question: Investigations into the illegal secret slaughtering of animals in Sicily have revealed that, with the complicity of supervisory authorities1, vast organised crime gangs are compromising the integrity of the CAP and putting consumers’ health at risk2.

The involvement of these criminal networks in the embezzlement of EU funds both violates EU financial regulations and has triggered a health emergency while posing a public health risk owing to the illegal slaughtering of animals and sale of infected meat3. An evident violation of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 and Regulation (EU) No 2021/2116.

According to press articles4, a detailed investigative report into these facts in the abattoir sector drafted by a committee of inquiry specially constituted by governmental decree56 was supressed in 2015 and has yet to see the light of day. Can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the regional authority's suppressed report on CAP fund fraud and, if so, does it intend to launch an in-depth investigation together with the relevant authorities?
Does it intend to take action to address these illegal activities and subsequently claw back funds?
Does it intend to strengthen Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 with a view to safeguarding public health against the risks of the slaughter and distribution of infected meat?

Top management of the Messina provincial health authority, the Animal Disease Institute (‘Istituto Zooprofilattico’), the Epidemiological Observatory on the Animal Sector and the region’s Department for Health and Epidemiological Observatory (DASOE) According to official data from the provincial health authority (ASP), there has been a resurgence of tuberculosis outbreaks in the Messina area. https://www.rainews.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.10.2024) The Commission has not been aware of such ‘regional authority's suppressed report on the common agricultural policy fund fraud’ and cannot thus currently comment on any related misuse of funds.

When the Commission becomes aware of any suspected cases of fraud, corruption or any other illegal activity affecting the EU budget, it informs the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF). OLAF analyses information of potential investigative interest to determine whether there are sufficient grounds to open an investigation.

OLAF can carry out administrative investigations when there are suspicions of fraud, corruption or other illegal activities against the financial interests of the EU. In addition, in case of criminal conduct in respect of which the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) could exercise its competence, the case is reported to the EPPO, who can initiate a criminal investigation.
From a food safety perspective, the current EU legal framework is considered fit for purpose. Its implementation and enforcement remain under the responsibility of the Member States.

Italian authorities have neither informed the Commission nor other Member States within the Alert and Cooperation Network (ACN)1 about the illegal slaughter of animals or the sale of meat unfit for human consumption in relation with the situation described. This absence of communication would conform with the EU legislation if the issue remains strictly limited to the Italian territory.
